title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a lower bound for the annealed complexity of a generalized spin glass model where the disorder couplings are Gaussian-divisible. By extending techniques from the purely Gaussian case, the authors prove that the complexity remains bounded below by the standard Gaussian result under specific conditions on the non-Gaussian disorder component. This advances the understanding of complexity measures in disordered quantum/classical systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine a universal lower bound for the annealed complexity of spin glass models whose disorder couplings are Gaussian-divisible rather than purely Gaussian.
main_result: The annealed complexity of the Gaussian-divisible model is shown to be at least the complexity of the standard Gaussian model, provided the non-Gaussian component is centered and subexponential.
method: The analysis heavily relies on the Kac–Rice formula to relate the expected number of critical points to integrals involving the Hamiltonian and its derivatives, followed by careful bounding of expectations involving non-Gaussian random variables.
model_or_system: The model is a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model characterized by a Hamiltonian involving $p$-spin interactions. The key feature is that the interaction coefficients are 'Gaussian-divisible,' meaning they are sums of a standard Gaussian variable and an independent, non-Gaussian variable.
key_observables: Annealed complexity, $\Theta_{N,p,\mu}(u)$, which measures the exponential growth rate of the expected number of critical points of the Hamiltonian lying in $(-\infty, u)$.
important_parameters: The disorder measure $\mu$ must be Gaussian-divisible, and the non-Gaussian part must be centered and subexponential. The analysis focuses on the limit $N 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The primary technical assumption is the subexponential nature of the non-Gaussian component. A limitation noted is that the lower bound proof is only rigorously established for delocalized vectors on the sphere.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon known results for the standard Gaussian model, extending the analysis using the Gaussian-divisible structure. It employs the Kac-Rice formula and decomposes the expectation calculation by conditioning on the non-Gaussian part to establish the lower bound.
why_interesting: While focused on classical spin glasses, the techniques developed for bounding complexity in disordered systems are highly relevant to understanding the energy landscapes and complexity measures in quantum many-body systems, especially those exhibiting glassy behavior.
